_metadata.title: Cluevoyance Unlimited pair library
_metadata.statuses: candidate | ai_reviewed | held | rejected | human_approved (never set by scripts)

pairs.pairNote: HEIST carries the pair alone; VAULT and SAFE are the same bank-side idea with diamond as an afterthought.

clues.wordAConnection: The bank job is the classic heist.
clues.wordBConnection: So is the diamond heist.
clues.revealExplanation: The diamond heist and the bank job are the same film plot.

blindReview.reason: Bank heist and diamond heist are both stock movie phrases.

clues.wordAConnection: The vault is the room at the heart of a bank.
clues.wordBConnection: Diamonds are what get locked in one.
clues.revealExplanation: Diamonds are kept in a bank vault.

blindReview.reason: Bank vault is direct; diamonds being kept in a vault is plausible but not a phrase anyone reaches for.

clues.wordAConnection: A safe is what a bank keeps things in.
clues.wordBConnection: A diamond is what goes in it.
clues.revealExplanation: A diamond goes in a safe and the safe goes in a bank.

blindReview.reason: A safe belongs to a bank; a diamond in a safe is only an inferred location.

pairs.pairNote: Two strong hints from different angles; TRUST is abstract on both sides.

clues.wordAConnection: A blood bank is where it is stored.
clues.wordBConnection: The heart is the pump that moves it.
clues.revealExplanation: A blood bank stores the blood the heart pumps.

blindReview.reason: Blood bank is a common phrase and the heart pumps blood.

clues.wordAConnection: You steal from a bank.
clues.wordBConnection: You steal someone's heart.
clues.revealExplanation: You steal from a bank and you steal someone's heart.

blindReview.reason: Robbers steal from banks and someone 'steals your heart'.

clues.wordAConnection: A trust is a banking arrangement.
clues.wordBConnection: Trust is a matter of the heart.
clues.revealExplanation: A trust is a banking arrangement and trust is a matter of the heart.

blindReview.reason: Trust companies and 'trust your heart' are each one step removed.

pairs.pairNote: Nothing clean here; each hint is a real pun on one side and a strained one on the other.

clues.wordAConnection: A bank is supposed to be financially stable.
clues.wordBConnection: A stable is where a horse is kept.
clues.revealExplanation: A stable is where a horse is kept and a bank is supposed to be financially stable.

blindReview.reason: Horse stable is direct; a 'stable bank' is an adjective use a player may not connect.

clues.wordAConnection: Bank charges are the fees on your account.
clues.wordBConnection: A horse charges into battle.
clues.revealExplanation: A horse charges into battle and bank charges are the fees on your account.

blindReview.reason: A bank charge is direct; a cavalry charge reaches horse only by a step.

clues.wordAConnection: You bank on a sure thing.
clues.wordBConnection: You bet on a horse.
clues.revealExplanation: You bet on a horse and you bank on a sure thing; both are staking money on an outcome.

blindReview.reason: Betting on horses is direct; bank as the house or bankroll in gambling is a stretch.

pairs.pairNote: PIG is clever and the closest to passing, but pig iron is half-obscure; BAR and SAFE each reach only one word with confidence.

clues.wordAConnection: Banks hold gold bars.
clues.wordBConnection: Iron bars are what keep a vault shut.
clues.revealExplanation: Banks hold gold bars and iron bars are what keep a vault shut.

blindReview.reason: Iron bar is direct; gold bars in a bank is an inferred image and there is no 'bank bar' phrase.

clues.wordAConnection: A piggy bank is the first bank anyone owns.
clues.wordBConnection: Pig iron is the raw cast metal.
clues.revealExplanation: Pig iron is the raw cast metal and a piggy bank is the first bank anyone owns.

blindReview.reason: Piggy bank is a familiar near-compound, but 'pig iron' is a term most non-specialists have at best heard of and could not place.

clues.wordAConnection: A bank safe is the box in the wall.
clues.wordBConnection: It is a box of thick iron.
clues.revealExplanation: A bank safe is a box of thick iron.

blindReview.reason: Bank safe is direct; iron as the material of a safe is a secondary thought.

pairs.pairNote: All three hints sit on the security idea but each reaches only one word cleanly; the pair lacks a real double meaning.

clues.wordAConnection: The vault is the room at the heart of a bank.
clues.wordBConnection: It is the thing a key is needed for.
clues.revealExplanation: A bank vault is the thing a key is needed for.

blindReview.reason: Bank vault is direct; a key for the vault is an inferred detail.

clues.wordAConnection: A safe deposit box sits in a bank.
clues.wordBConnection: It opens with the customer's own key.
clues.revealExplanation: A safe deposit box sits in a bank and opens with the customer's own key.

blindReview.reason: Bank deposit is direct; 'key deposit' is a real but unfamiliar phrase and the safe-deposit-box key is a thin reach.

clues.wordAConnection: A bank locks its money away.
clues.wordBConnection: A key is what opens a lock.
clues.revealExplanation: A bank locks its money away and a key is what opens a lock.

blindReview.reason: Lock and key is direct; lock to bank goes through vault or lockbox.

pairs.pairNote: MAN (Batman / Spider-Man) and HANG are both clean; HALLOWEEN and CREEPY are natural shared associations; WEB and WINGS are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: Paper bats on Halloween.
clues.wordBConnection: Fake spiders and cobwebs on Halloween.
clues.revealExplanation: Both are Halloween decorations.

blindReview.reason: Bats and spiders (with their cobwebs) are both standard Halloween decorations; the holiday is natural to each word.

clues.wordAConnection: Bats hang upside down to roost.
clues.wordBConnection: A spider hangs from its thread.
clues.revealExplanation: Bats hang upside down; spiders hang by a thread.

blindReview.reason: Bats hang upside down and spiders hang from their threads; both are plain-sense and direct.

clues.wordAConnection: Batman.
clues.wordBConnection: Spider-Man.
clues.revealExplanation: Batman and Spider-Man.

blindReview.reason: Judged as compounds: Batman and Spider-Man, two of the most famous superheroes in the US; each is a direct hit.

clues.wordAConnection: A bat is the creepy creature of the night.
clues.wordBConnection: A spider is the original creepy-crawly.
clues.revealExplanation: Both are famously creepy.

provenance.authorReason: a mood word; fits half the board

blindReview.reason: Spiders are the archetypal creepy-crawly and bats are a stock creepy creature of the night; a mood word, but natural to both.
Bats live in caves and 'Batcave' is famous; cave spiders exist but are a stretch for the spider side.
Web is the spider's signature; bats do not reach it.
Bats have wings; spiders do not.

pairs.pairNote: The dental double meaning carries the pair, though both PASS hints are the same idea; ARCH does not reach crown.

clues.wordAConnection: A bridge is one of the things a dentist fits.
clues.wordBConnection: A crown is the other.
clues.revealExplanation: A crown and a bridge are both things a dentist fits in your mouth.

blindReview.reason: A dentist fits both bridges and crowns; the dental sense is familiar to most US adults.

clues.wordAConnection: A bridge spans the gap where teeth are missing.
clues.wordBConnection: A crown caps the one that is left.
clues.revealExplanation: A crown caps one tooth and a bridge spans the gap where others are missing.

blindReview.reason: A tooth gets a crown or is replaced by a bridge; same dental idea as DENTIST.

clues.wordAConnection: London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme.
clues.wordBConnection: The Crown Jewels are in the Tower of London.
clues.revealExplanation: London Bridge is in the nursery rhyme and the Crown Jewels are in the Tower of London: the city's name is attached to both.

reference.source: London Bridge and the Crown Jewels

blindReview.reason: London Bridge is direct; the Crown Jewels or the British Crown is a looser association.

clues.wordAConnection: An arch is what holds a stone bridge up.
clues.wordBConnection: The crown is the architect's name for the very top of it.
clues.revealExplanation: An arch is what holds a stone bridge up, and the crown is the architect's name for the very top of it.

blindReview.reason: Arch bridge is direct, but the 'crown' of an arch is an architecture term nobody outside the trade uses.

pairs.pairNote: BURN is the obvious hint and CROSS a fair compound play; LONDON is bridge-first with fire attached by a history lesson.

clues.wordAConnection: To burn your bridges is the idiom.
clues.wordBConnection: Burning is what fire does.
clues.revealExplanation: To burn your bridges is the idiom, and burning is what fire does.

blindReview.reason: 'Burn your bridges' is a universal idiom and fire burns.

clues.wordAConnection: Crossing is what a bridge is for.
clues.wordBConnection: Crossfire is what you get caught in.
clues.revealExplanation: Crossfire is what you get caught in and crossing is what a bridge is for.

blindReview.reason: Cross a bridge is direct and crossfire is a familiar compound; judged as compounds both sides are reached.

clues.wordAConnection: London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme.
clues.wordBConnection: The Great Fire of London is the city's other famous story.
clues.revealExplanation: London Bridge is the one in the nursery rhyme and the Great Fire of London is the city's other famous story.

reference.source: London Bridge and the Great Fire of London

blindReview.reason: London Bridge is famous; the Great Fire of London is history many US adults will not recall in time.

pairs.pairNote: Two good hints of different flavors; GAP is bridge-only.

clues.wordAConnection: Bridge is a card game.
clues.wordBConnection: Hearts is one of its four suits.
clues.revealExplanation: Hearts is a card suit and bridge is a card game.

blindReview.reason: Bridge is a card game and hearts is a card suit and game.

clues.wordAConnection: Crossing is what a bridge is for.
clues.wordBConnection: Cross my heart is the promise.
clues.revealExplanation: Cross my heart is the promise and crossing is what a bridge is for.

blindReview.reason: Cross a bridge and 'cross my heart' are both everyday phrases.

clues.wordAConnection: A bridge closes a gap.
clues.wordBConnection: A hole in the heart is a gap surgeons close.
clues.revealExplanation: A bridge closes a gap and a hole in the heart is a gap surgeons close.

blindReview.reason: Bridge the gap is direct; there is no natural route from gap to heart.

pairs.pairNote: A hard pair with no fair hint; GOLDEN is the best of a weak set and still a colour clue plus a landmark name.

clues.wordAConnection: A bridge is what the dentist fits once the teeth have gone.
clues.wordBConnection: Honey is what a sweet tooth wants.
clues.revealExplanation: Honey is what a sweet tooth wants and a bridge is what the dentist fits once the teeth have gone.

blindReview.reason: Dental bridge is direct; honey is reached only via 'sweet tooth', which is not a compound with honey.

clues.wordAConnection: The Golden Gate is the most famous bridge there is.
clues.wordBConnection: Golden is the standard word for honey.
clues.revealExplanation: The Golden Gate is the most famous bridge there is, and golden is the standard word for honey.

blindReview.reason: Honey is golden; 'golden bridge' is not a phrase, so bridge is reached only by completing the Golden Gate name.

clues.wordAConnection: Poohsticks is the game you play from a bridge.
clues.wordBConnection: Pooh wants honey above everything else.
clues.revealExplanation: Winnie-the-Pooh wants honey above everything, and Poohsticks is the game you play from a bridge.

blindReview.reason: Pooh and honey are inseparable, but the Poohsticks bridge is a detail almost no US adult will summon.

clues.wordAConnection: The Rainbow Bridge is the crossing over the gorge.
clues.wordBConnection: Niagara is where honeymooners go.
clues.revealExplanation: Niagara is where honeymooners go, and the Rainbow Bridge is the crossing that takes you over the gorge to get there.

blindReview.reason: Rainbow Bridge at Niagara and Niagara as honeymoon capital are both trivia; neither side is reachable cold.

pairs.pairNote: SONG is a clean double meaning and STONE a fair compound play; ISLAND needs the player to assemble the link.

clues.wordAConnection: A song has a bridge in the middle.
clues.wordBConnection: And it is written in a key.
clues.revealExplanation: A song has a bridge in the middle and is written in a key.

blindReview.reason: A song has a bridge section and is written in a key; both are common musical terms.

clues.wordAConnection: A stone bridge stands on its arch.
clues.wordBConnection: The keystone is the wedge at the top that holds the arch shut.
clues.revealExplanation: A stone bridge stands on its arch, and the keystone is the wedge at the top that holds the arch shut.

blindReview.reason: Stone bridge is a natural phrase and keystone a familiar compound; a bonus is that the keystone is itself part of an arch bridge.

clues.wordAConnection: Bridges are what string the Florida Keys together.
clues.wordBConnection: A key is a low-lying island.
clues.revealExplanation: A key is a low-lying island and bridges are what string the Florida Keys together.

blindReview.reason: Key as island (Florida Keys) and a bridge to an island are each one stretch; neither side is direct.

pairs.pairNote: CHASE is the most natural plain-sense hint; TOM and JERRY are one cartoon idea; WHISKERS passes as a shared animal feature; CHEESE, CLICK and TRAP are mouse-only.

clues.wordAConnection: The cat does the chasing.
clues.wordBConnection: The mouse gets chased.
clues.revealExplanation: The classic chase: cat after mouse.

blindReview.reason: The cat is the chaser and the mouse the chased in the universal 'cat and mouse' chase; the association is natural to both words.

clues.wordAConnection: Tom is a cat (and a tomcat is a male cat).
clues.wordBConnection: Tom's whole life is chasing Jerry the mouse.
clues.revealExplanation: Tom the cat and Jerry the mouse.

blindReview.reason: A tom is a male cat in plain English and Tom is the cartoon cat; MOUSE arrives through his nemesis Jerry, a widely known pairing.

clues.wordAConnection: Jerry is forever chased by Tom the cat.
clues.wordBConnection: Jerry is the mouse.
clues.revealExplanation: Jerry the mouse, and Tom the cat who chases him.

blindReview.reason: Jerry is the Tom and Jerry mouse; CAT follows from his cartoon rival, a pairing most US adults know.

clues.wordAConnection: A cat's whiskers.
clues.wordBConnection: A mouse's whiskers.
clues.revealExplanation: Both animals twitch their whiskers.

blindReview.reason: Whiskers are the cat's signature, and mice are also drawn and described by their whiskers (twitching whiskers, cartoon mice); natural to both animals.

provenance.authorReason: generic: every mammal on the board has paws

blindReview.reason: Paws are a cat staple; mice do have paws but it is not a natural association for the mouse, so the second side needs prompting.
Cheese is the classic mouse bait; it says nothing about a cat.
Click is the computer-mouse sense; there is no cat sense of click.

provenance.authorReason: mousetrap is direct; the cat side needs an explanation

blindReview.reason: Mousetrap is immediate; calling a cat a 'trap' for mice is an explanation, not a connection, and 'cat trap' is not a compound.

pairs.pairNote: SALEM has two independent routes; FAMILIAR is a smart plain-sense hint; HALLOWEEN and BLACK are natural easy hints; BINX is accurate but niche.

clues.wordAConnection: Salem is the cat in Sabrina.
clues.wordBConnection: The Salem witch trials.
clues.revealExplanation: Salem: the witch trials, and Sabrina's cat.

reference.source: Salem witch trials / Sabrina the Teenage Witch

blindReview.reason: Salem is the town of the witch trials and the talking black cat in Sabrina the Teenage Witch; two genuinely separate routes.

clues.wordAConnection: The Halloween black cat.
clues.wordBConnection: The Halloween witch.
clues.revealExplanation: Both are Halloween figures.

blindReview.reason: Witch is a top Halloween icon and the black cat is a canonical Halloween image; natural to both.

clues.wordAConnection: A witch's familiar is usually a cat.
clues.wordBConnection: The witch's familiar: her animal companion.
clues.revealExplanation: A witch's familiar, the cat at her side.

provenance.authorReason: a term of art on the witch side, plain word on the cat side

blindReview.reason: A familiar is a witch's animal spirit in the occult sense, and the archetypal familiar is a cat; the everyday 'well-known' sense may distract some players.

clues.wordAConnection: A black cat.
clues.wordBConnection: The witch in black with her black cat.
clues.revealExplanation: A witch and her black cat.

blindReview.reason: Black cat is immediate, and black is the witch's colour (black hat, black robes, black magic); a natural easy hint for both.
Thackery Binx is the black cat cursed by the Sanderson witches in Hocus Pocus (1993); real, but the name is known mainly to fans of that film.

provenance.authorReason: WITCH only; the cat is one more hop

blindReview.reason: Sabrina the Teenage Witch is well known; CAT comes only from remembering her cat Salem.
Broom is the witch's vehicle; cats have no claim on it.

pairs.pairNote: HAMLET is the ideal single-reference hint for those who know the play; CASTLE is the plain-sense fallback.

clues.wordAConnection: Hamlet is a play about a stolen crown.
clues.wordBConnection: It opens with the ghost of the dead king.
clues.revealExplanation: Hamlet opens with the ghost of a king demanding his stolen crown be avenged.

blindReview.reason: Hamlet is a prince fighting over a stolen crown and is driven by his father's ghost; both are the play's core.

clues.wordAConnection: The castle is where the crown lives.
clues.wordBConnection: And where its ghosts are said to walk.
clues.revealExplanation: The castle is where the crown lives and where its ghosts are said to walk.

blindReview.reason: Haunted castle is a stock image and a castle is where crowned royalty live.

clues.wordAConnection: A king wears the crown.
clues.wordBConnection: The ghost of a dead king is the oldest story there is.
clues.revealExplanation: A king wears the crown and the ghost of a dead king is the oldest story there is.

blindReview.reason: King to crown is immediate; king to ghost needs Hamlet's ghost king or a Stephen King detour.

pairs.pairNote: QUEEN is the stronger of two near-identical royal-card hints; CARD is heart-first.

clues.wordAConnection: A queen is who wears the crown.
clues.wordBConnection: The Queen of Hearts is the card.
clues.revealExplanation: The Queen of Hearts is the card and a queen is who wears the crown.

blindReview.reason: A queen wears a crown and the Queen of Hearts is a famous card and character.

clues.wordAConnection: A king is crowned.
clues.wordBConnection: The King of Hearts is in every deck.
clues.revealExplanation: The King of Hearts is in every deck and a king is crowned.

blindReview.reason: A king wears a crown and the King of Hearts is a playing card.

clues.wordAConnection: The crowned royals are the face cards.
clues.wordBConnection: Hearts is one of the four suits.
clues.revealExplanation: Hearts is a card suit and the crowned royals are the face cards.

blindReview.reason: Hearts is a suit; crown only via the pictures on face cards.

pairs.pairNote: No fair hint; QUEEN is the only one that even gestures at both words.

clues.wordAConnection: A queen is who wears the crown.
clues.wordBConnection: The queen bee rules the hive that makes the honey.
clues.revealExplanation: The queen bee rules the hive that makes the honey and a queen is who wears the crown.

blindReview.reason: Queen to crown is immediate; honey needs queen bee and then the hive, two steps.

clues.wordAConnection: Royal is what a crown makes you.
clues.wordBConnection: Royal jelly is what the hive feeds its future queen.
clues.revealExplanation: Royal jelly is what the hive feeds its future queen, and royal is what a crown makes you.

blindReview.reason: Royal to crown is direct; royal jelly is a bee product, not honey, and is obscure anyway.

clues.wordAConnection: Mead is what got drunk in the crowned head's hall.
clues.wordBConnection: Mead is wine made from honey.
clues.revealExplanation: Mead is wine made from honey and it is what got drunk in the crowned head's hall.

blindReview.reason: Mead is honey wine for those who know it, but nothing about mead points to a crown.

pairs.pairNote: No clean hint: all three reach one side strongly and the other only by a figurative or etymological step.

clues.wordAConnection: The Statue of Liberty wears a spiked crown.
clues.wordBConnection: And holds up a torch of light.
clues.revealExplanation: The Statue of Liberty wears a spiked crown and holds up a torch of light.

blindReview.reason: The Statue of Liberty's spiked crown is iconic; light comes only through her torch and that is a second step.

clues.wordAConnection: A halo sits exactly where a crown would.
clues.wordBConnection: A halo is a ring of light.
clues.revealExplanation: A halo is a ring of light that sits exactly where a crown would.

blindReview.reason: A halo is a ring of light; calling it a crown is a shape analogy, not a phrase a stranger reaches for.

clues.wordAConnection: Corona is Latin for crown, which is where coronation comes from.
clues.wordBConnection: The sun's corona is a ring of light.
clues.revealExplanation: Corona is Latin for crown, which is where coronation comes from, and the sun's corona is a ring of light.

blindReview.reason: The sun's corona is a crown of light, but corona meaning crown is Latin most US players know only via beer or the virus.

pairs.pairNote: An unnatural pairing; CURSE is the only hint with a foothold on both words and it is weak.

clues.wordAConnection: The Hope Diamond is supposed to be cursed.
clues.wordBConnection: And to have haunted everyone who owned it.
clues.revealExplanation: The Hope Diamond is supposed to be cursed and to have haunted everyone who owned it.

blindReview.reason: Cursed diamonds (Hope Diamond) and curses bringing ghosts are each a stretch.

clues.wordAConnection: A stolen diamond vanishes overnight.
clues.wordBConnection: So does a ghost.
clues.revealExplanation: A stolen diamond vanishes overnight and so does a ghost.

blindReview.reason: Ghosts vanish; a diamond vanishing is only a heist plot, not a property of diamonds.

clues.wordAConnection: The Tower of London holds the great diamonds.
clues.wordBConnection: And Britain's most famous ghosts.
clues.revealExplanation: The Tower of London holds the great diamonds and Britain's most famous ghosts.

blindReview.reason: A haunted tower is a loose image and tower to diamond requires knowing the Crown Jewels sit in the Tower of London.

pairs.pairNote: CUT is a satisfying double meaning and LOVE a natural generic; PINK is a colour hint that favors rose.

clues.wordAConnection: The rose cut is a genuine antique style of cutting a diamond.
clues.wordBConnection: It is named after the flower it resembles.
clues.revealExplanation: The rose cut is a genuine antique style of cutting a diamond.

blindReview.reason: A diamond's cut is its key quality and cut roses are what florists sell.

clues.wordAConnection: A diamond ring is one way of saying it.
clues.wordBConnection: A dozen roses is the other.
clues.revealExplanation: A dozen roses and a diamond ring are two ways of saying the same thing.

blindReview.reason: Diamond rings and roses are the two standard tokens of love.

clues.wordAConnection: A pink diamond is the rarest kind.
clues.wordBConnection: Pink is the colour of a rose.
clues.revealExplanation: A pink diamond is the rarest kind and pink is the colour of a rose.

blindReview.reason: Pink roses are everywhere; pink diamonds exist but are a specialist thought.

pairs.pairNote: Excellent pair; all three hints are direct on both sides.

clues.wordAConnection: A diamond is a crystal nobody can grow.
clues.wordBConnection: Salt is the one you can grow on a string.
clues.revealExplanation: Salt and diamond are both crystals, one you can grow on a string and one you cannot.

blindReview.reason: Diamond is a crystal and salt forms crystals; both direct.

clues.wordAConnection: A big diamond gets called a rock.
clues.wordBConnection: Rock salt is what goes on the roads.
clues.revealExplanation: Rock salt is what goes on the roads and a rock is what a big diamond gets called.

blindReview.reason: Rock salt is a product name and a diamond is a 'rock' in everyday slang.

clues.wordAConnection: Diamonds are dug out of mines.
clues.wordBConnection: So is salt.
clues.revealExplanation: Salt and diamonds are both dug out of mines.

blindReview.reason: Diamond mine and salt mine are both familiar phrases.

pairs.pairNote: The pair is really the word 'diamondback', and BACK is the hint that invokes it; PATTERN and SCALE each favor one side.

clues.wordAConnection: A diamondback is named for the diamonds down its back.
clues.wordBConnection: And a diamondback is a rattlesnake.
clues.revealExplanation: A diamondback is a rattlesnake, named for the diamonds running down its back.

blindReview.reason: Judged as a compound, diamondback is a familiar word and it names a rattlesnake, so one compound reaches both words; snake is one step behind diamond.

clues.wordAConnection: The pattern on the skin is diamonds.
clues.wordBConnection: The skin is a snake's.
clues.revealExplanation: A snake's skin is patterned in diamonds.

blindReview.reason: Diamond pattern is a stock phrase; snakeskin pattern is a secondary association, so the snake side is the weak one.

clues.wordAConnection: A cut stone's facets are diamond-shaped.
clues.wordBConnection: So are the scales down a snake.
clues.revealExplanation: Snake scales are diamond-shaped and overlap like a cut stone's facets.

blindReview.reason: Snake scales are direct; diamond to scale requires the Mohs hardness or carat scale.

pairs.pairNote: Three natural plain-sense hints; DOGFISH is disqualified; TANK and FETCH are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: A dog's food bowl.
clues.wordBConnection: A fish bowl.
clues.revealExplanation: Dog bowl, fish bowl.

blindReview.reason: Dog bowl and fishbowl are both everyday phrases.

clues.wordAConnection: The classic pet.
clues.wordBConnection: A pet fish in its bowl.
clues.revealExplanation: Both are everyday pets.

provenance.authorReason: generic: cat, mouse and more are pets too

blindReview.reason: The dog is the archetypal pet and 'pet fish' is an everyday phrase; natural to both.

clues.wordAConnection: A dog with a bone.
clues.wordBConnection: Fish bones.
clues.revealExplanation: A dog's bone and a fish bone.

blindReview.reason: Dog bone is immediate and fish bones / fishbone are everyday.
The hint literally contains both target words.
Fish tank is direct; no dog sense.
Fetch is a dog game; fish do not play it.

pairs.pairNote: ROLL and EASTER are clean two-way hints and CHICK is a good third; COIL, YOLK and SCRAMBLE are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: An egg roll.
clues.wordBConnection: A spring roll.
clues.revealExplanation: Egg roll, spring roll.

blindReview.reason: Egg roll and spring roll are both everyday menu items.

clues.wordAConnection: Easter eggs.
clues.wordBConnection: Easter falls in spring.
clues.revealExplanation: Easter eggs, in spring.

blindReview.reason: Easter eggs are iconic and Easter is the spring holiday.

clues.wordAConnection: A chick hatches from an egg.
clues.wordBConnection: Spring chicks.
clues.revealExplanation: Spring is when chicks hatch from their eggs.

blindReview.reason: A chick hatches from an egg; chicks are a spring/Easter symbol and 'spring chicken' is an idiom, a solid second reach.
Eggs sit in nests (and 'nest egg'); nesting happens in spring but that is seasonal background rather than a direct link.
A coil is a spring; eggs do not coil.
Yolk is pure egg; nothing on the spring side.
Scrambled eggs are immediate; no spring sense.

pairs.pairNote: Solid pair; all three hints reach both words without explanation.

clues.wordAConnection: Fire burns.
clues.wordBConnection: Heartburn is the familiar complaint.
clues.revealExplanation: Fire burns, and heartburn is the familiar complaint.

blindReview.reason: Fire burns directly; heartburn is an everyday compound, judged as such.

clues.wordAConnection: Passion is always described as fiery.
clues.wordBConnection: The heart is its traditional seat.
clues.revealExplanation: Passion is described as fiery, and the heart is its traditional seat.

blindReview.reason: Passion is fiery and heartfelt; a mood hint, but both metaphors are standard.

clues.wordAConnection: A fire keeps you warm.
clues.wordBConnection: Warm-hearted describes a kind person.
clues.revealExplanation: A fire keeps you warm and warm-hearted describes a kind person.

blindReview.reason: A warm fire and a warm heart are both everyday phrases.

pairs.pairNote: WILD is the only hint that reaches both sides without a story; TROJAN is horse-only in practice.

clues.wordAConnection: A wildfire is the one that gets away.
clues.wordBConnection: A wild horse is the one nobody has broken.
clues.revealExplanation: A wildfire and a wild horse both take the same modifier.

blindReview.reason: Wildfire and wild horse are both immediate.

clues.wordAConnection: Troy was sacked and burned.
clues.wordBConnection: The Trojan horse is how they got in.
clues.revealExplanation: The Trojan horse led to Troy being sacked and burned.

blindReview.reason: Trojan Horse is famous; fire only via the burning of Troy, which must be explained.

clues.wordAConnection: The branding iron is heated in a fire.
clues.wordBConnection: Horses are what get marked with it.
clues.revealExplanation: Horses are marked with a brand, and the branding iron is heated in a fire.

blindReview.reason: Firebrand gets partway to fire, but branding is associated with cattle far more than horses; both sides need a step.

pairs.pairNote: Strong pair; FORGE is the natural answer, HOT a safe backup, SMITH duplicates FORGE, and BRAND is the weakest PASS.

clues.wordAConnection: A forge is a contained fire.
clues.wordBConnection: Iron is what gets shaped in it.
clues.revealExplanation: Iron is shaped in a forge, which is a contained fire.

blindReview.reason: A forge is a fire used to heat and work iron; both sides are immediate.

clues.wordAConnection: Fire is the definition of hot.
clues.wordBConnection: Strike while the iron is hot is the saying.
clues.revealExplanation: Fire is hot, and the saying is to strike while the iron is hot.

blindReview.reason: Fire is hot, and 'hot iron' / 'strike while the iron is hot' is a standard phrase; generic but natural to both.

clues.wordAConnection: A blacksmith works by fire.
clues.wordBConnection: Iron is what he works.
clues.revealExplanation: A blacksmith works iron using fire.

blindReview.reason: A blacksmith works iron (direct) at a fire (one step via the forge); same idea as FORGE.

clues.wordAConnection: A branding iron is heated in a fire.
clues.wordBConnection: And the brand itself is a piece of iron.
clues.revealExplanation: A branding iron is heated in a fire before it is used.

blindReview.reason: Branding iron is direct; fire comes through the familiar compound firebrand and the older sense of a burning stick.

pairs.pairNote: Very easy pair; every hint works, with CANDLE and TORCH resting on the same burning-light-source idea.

clues.wordAConnection: A match starts a fire.
clues.wordBConnection: And is struck to make light.
clues.revealExplanation: A match starts a fire and is struck to make light.

blindReview.reason: A match starts a fire and you 'light a match'; both senses immediate.

clues.wordAConnection: A torch is a burning brand.
clues.wordBConnection: And the everyday word for a hand-held light.
clues.revealExplanation: A torch is a burning brand and also the everyday word for a hand-held light.

blindReview.reason: A torch is burning fire carried for light; torchlight is a common word.

clues.wordAConnection: A spark is what sets a fire going.
clues.wordBConnection: And it is a flash of light.
clues.revealExplanation: A spark is a flash of light and the thing that sets a fire going.

blindReview.reason: A spark ignites fire and is itself a tiny flash of light.

clues.wordAConnection: A candle is a small contained fire.
clues.wordBConnection: Kept specifically for its light.
clues.revealExplanation: A candle is a small contained fire kept specifically for its light.

blindReview.reason: Candlelight is direct; candle to fire goes through the flame, one small step.

pairs.pairNote: FINGER is the one hint that compounds on both sides; SCALES, BOWL and NUGGET each need a second step on the gold or fish side; GOLDFISH is disqualified.

clues.heldReason: override: held out of the first US beta pending final content review: fish finger is the British term (US: fish sticks); the blind review passed it, so it stays in the library
clues.wordAConnection: Fish fingers.
clues.wordBConnection: Goldfinger.
clues.revealExplanation: Fish fingers and Goldfinger.

blindReview.reason: Judged as compounds: Goldfinger (the Bond film) is broadly known; 'fish finger' is the British term for a fish stick, which most US adults recognise even if they do not use it, so FISH is a solid if slightly foreign reach.

override.reason: held out of the first US beta pending final content review: fish finger is the British term (US: fish sticks); the blind review passed it, so it stays in the library

blindReview.reason: The hint literally contains both target words.
Fishbowl is immediate; there is no 'gold bowl' compound, so GOLD arrives only by routing through 'goldfish bowl'.

provenance.authorReason: GOLD only; chicken nugget, not fish

blindReview.reason: Gold nugget is the first sense; 'fish nugget' is a real but minor frozen-food term that few US players would produce.

clues.wordAConnection: Fish scales.
clues.wordBConnection: Gold is weighed on scales.
clues.revealExplanation: Fish scales, and the scales that weigh gold.

blindReview.reason: Fish scales are direct; weighing gold on scales is a real image (assayers, gold rush) but needs a nudge.
Treasure is gold; fish do not come up.
Gold rush is clear; there is no fish compound with rush.

pairs.pairNote: Two good hints; HEADLESS is the single-reference ideal, RIDER is a strong plain-sense plus pop-culture pair.

clues.wordAConnection: The Headless Horseman is the ghost.
clues.wordBConnection: And he never appears off his horse.
clues.revealExplanation: The Headless Horseman is a ghost on horseback.

blindReview.reason: The Headless Horseman is a ghost on a horse; one reference reaches both sides at once.

clues.wordAConnection: The phantom rider is the oldest shape a ghost story takes.
clues.wordBConnection: And he is always on horseback.
clues.revealExplanation: The phantom rider on his horse is the oldest shape a ghost story takes.

blindReview.reason: A rider rides a horse, and Ghost Rider (comics, film, Johnny Cash song) is a widely known phrase.

clues.wordAConnection: The name of the one who sat on it was Death.
clues.wordBConnection: Behold a pale horse.
clues.revealExplanation: Behold a pale horse, and the name of the one who sat on it was Death.

blindReview.reason: Ghosts are pale; the pale horse of Revelation is a reference many players will not make.

pairs.pairNote: SKELETON is an excellent hint; the other two are key-first.

clues.wordAConnection: A skeleton is what the haunted house keeps in its cupboard.
clues.wordBConnection: A skeleton key opens every door in it.
clues.revealExplanation: A skeleton key opens every door in the house and a skeleton is what the haunted house keeps in its cupboard.

blindReview.reason: Skeleton key is a common term and skeletons sit beside ghosts in every spooky lineup.

clues.wordAConnection: The haunted house is the ghost's address.
clues.wordBConnection: It gets handed over with one big rusted key.
clues.revealExplanation: The haunted house is handed over with one big rusted key.

blindReview.reason: House key is direct; ghost arrives only by adding 'haunted', since 'ghost house' is not the phrase.

clues.wordAConnection: A ghost simply walks through a locked door.
clues.wordBConnection: A key is what everybody else needs.
clues.revealExplanation: A key is what you need for a locked door and a ghost simply walks through it.

blindReview.reason: Locked points straight to key but nothing about it points to ghost.

pairs.pairNote: Every hint is light-first with ghost reached only through a haunting trope or a film title.

clues.wordAConnection: A flickering bulb is the standard film signal that a ghost has arrived.
clues.wordBConnection: Flickering is what a light does.
clues.revealExplanation: Lights flickering is the standard film signal that a ghost has arrived.

blindReview.reason: Lights flicker directly; flickering lights as a haunting sign is a trope the player must supply.

clues.wordAConnection: Ghost hunters photograph floating orbs and call them spirits.
clues.wordBConnection: An orb is a ball of light.
clues.revealExplanation: Ghost hunters photograph floating orbs of light and call them spirits.

blindReview.reason: An orb of light is direct; 'ghost orbs' are a ghost-hunting term unknown to most.

clues.wordAConnection: The Shining is the ghost story everyone knows.
clues.wordBConnection: Shining is what light does.
clues.revealExplanation: The Shining is the ghost story everyone knows, and shining is what light does.

blindReview.reason: Shining light is direct; The Shining is a famous ghost story but the title alone does not say ghost.

pairs.pairNote: TREASURE and DOUBLOON are both clean; COIN and TOOTH pass on natural pirate imagery; PARROT, PLANK and MEDAL are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: A doubloon is a gold coin.
clues.wordBConnection: The pirate's coin of choice.
clues.revealExplanation: Doubloons: the pirate's gold coins.

blindReview.reason: A doubloon is a Spanish gold coin and the word lives almost entirely in pirate stories; slightly bookish but well known.

clues.wordAConnection: A treasure of gold.
clues.wordBConnection: Pirates bury treasure.
clues.revealExplanation: Pirate treasure: gold.

blindReview.reason: Treasure means gold in the popular imagination and pirate treasure is the archetype.

clues.wordAConnection: A gold coin.
clues.wordBConnection: The pirate's chest of coins.
clues.revealExplanation: Gold coins, the pirate's haul.

blindReview.reason: Gold coin is immediate; the pirate's chest of coins is a natural image for the pirate side.

clues.wordAConnection: A gold tooth.
clues.wordBConnection: The pirate's gold tooth.
clues.revealExplanation: The pirate's gold tooth.

blindReview.reason: Gold tooth is a stock phrase and the gold-toothed pirate is a stereotype; the pirate side depends on that one image.
Pirate booty is immediate; booty means plunder, which implies gold only loosely.
Parrot on the shoulder is pure pirate; no gold link.
Walking the plank is pirate-only.
Gold medal is direct; pirates do not win medals.

pairs.pairNote: PUMP and BLOOD are both excellent; CORE and COLD are weaker and lean on one side.

clues.wordAConnection: The heart is what pumps it round.
clues.wordBConnection: Blood is red because of the iron in it.
clues.revealExplanation: Blood is red because of the iron in it and the heart is what pumps it round.

blindReview.reason: The heart pumps blood and blood contains iron; both facts are common knowledge.

clues.wordAConnection: The heart is a pump.
clues.wordBConnection: Pumping iron is what you do at the gym.
clues.revealExplanation: The heart is a pump and pumping iron is what you do at the gym.

blindReview.reason: The heart is a pump and 'pump iron' means lifting weights.

clues.wordAConnection: A cold heart is one with no feeling in it.
clues.wordBConnection: Iron is cold to the touch.
clues.revealExplanation: Iron is cold to the touch and a cold heart is one with no feeling in it.

blindReview.reason: Cold heart is direct; 'cold iron' is a literary phrase few would reach for.

clues.wordAConnection: Core is heart in Latin.
clues.wordBConnection: The earth's core is solid iron.
clues.revealExplanation: Core is heart in Latin, and the earth's core is solid iron.

blindReview.reason: Heart as the core of something and Earth's iron core are each a step away.

pairs.pairNote: A gentle pair where NECTAR bridges both words; BEE and SWEET are honey-first.

clues.wordAConnection: Nectar is what becomes honey.
clues.wordBConnection: A rose is what holds it.
clues.revealExplanation: A rose holds nectar and nectar is what becomes honey.

blindReview.reason: Honey is made from nectar and nectar is what a flower like a rose holds; the flower link is the natural next thought.

clues.wordAConnection: Honey is what comes of it.
clues.wordBConnection: Bees work the roses.
clues.revealExplanation: Bees work the roses and honey is what comes of it.

blindReview.reason: Bees make honey; a bee visiting a rose is incidental.

clues.wordAConnection: Honey is sweet.
clues.wordBConnection: A rose is the sweetest thing in the garden to smell.
clues.revealExplanation: Honey is sweet and a rose is the sweetest thing in the garden to smell.

blindReview.reason: Honey is sweet; a rose smelling sweet is poetic rather than immediate, so the rose side is the weak one.

pairs.pairNote: SWEET works through contrast; LICK and CURE are salt-first with honey tacked on.

clues.wordAConnection: Honey is sweetness itself.
clues.wordBConnection: Salt is its exact opposite on the tongue.
clues.revealExplanation: Honey is sweetness itself and salt is its exact opposite on the tongue.

blindReview.reason: Honey is sweet and 'sweet and salty' is such a fixed pairing that salt is reachable as the contrast.

clues.wordAConnection: Honey is licked off the spoon.
clues.wordBConnection: A salt lick is put out in the field.
clues.revealExplanation: A salt lick is put out in the field and honey is licked off the spoon.

blindReview.reason: Salt lick is a set phrase; licking honey is just something one might do.

clues.wordAConnection: Honey is the other preservative, the one that never spoils.
clues.wordBConnection: Salt is what cures the meat.
clues.revealExplanation: Salt cures meat and honey is the other preservative that never spoils.

blindReview.reason: Salt cures meat; honey-cured or honey as a folk remedy is a secondary thought.

pairs.pairNote: A soft pair; POLLEN is the one hint that sits between both words, while BEE and BLOSSOM each face one of them.

clues.wordAConnection: Pollen is what bees carry home alongside the nectar.
clues.wordBConnection: Spring is pollen season.
clues.revealExplanation: Spring is pollen season and pollen is what bees carry home alongside the nectar.

blindReview.reason: Pollen season is spring; bees gathering pollen to make honey is how most people picture honey-making.

clues.wordAConnection: The honey follows.
clues.wordBConnection: Bees come out in spring.
clues.revealExplanation: Bees come out in spring and the honey follows.

blindReview.reason: Bees make honey; bees being active in spring is seasonal background, not a link.

clues.wordAConnection: Blossom is the source of the nectar that becomes honey.
clues.wordBConnection: Spring is when it arrives.
clues.revealExplanation: Spring blossom is the source of the nectar that becomes honey.

blindReview.reason: Spring blossom is direct; honey from blossoms (orange blossom honey) is a secondary association.

pairs.pairNote: SMITH is the one defensible hint; SHOE is horse-only and TRAIN needs the 'iron horse' nickname.

clues.wordAConnection: The blacksmith shoes the horses.
clues.wordBConnection: And works the iron to do it.
clues.revealExplanation: The blacksmith works iron and shoes the horses.

blindReview.reason: A blacksmith works iron and the classic image is of him shoeing a horse.

clues.wordAConnection: A horseshoe is what gets nailed on.
clues.wordBConnection: And it is a bent bar of iron.
clues.revealExplanation: A horseshoe is a bent bar of iron.

blindReview.reason: Horseshoe is an immediate compound; there is no 'shoe + iron' compound, so iron is only reached by recalling the material.

clues.wordAConnection: The iron horse was what they called the steam train when it first appeared.
clues.wordBConnection: And it was built of iron.
clues.revealExplanation: The iron horse was what they called the steam train when it first appeared.

blindReview.reason: Both sides depend on knowing the nickname 'iron horse' for a locomotive, and TRAIN itself is not part of that compound.

pairs.pairNote: WAR works; DERBY and BLANKET both lean on the same obscure Kentucky Derby rose tradition.

clues.wordAConnection: A warhorse is what they were fought on.
clues.wordBConnection: The Wars of the Roses were fought over the badge.
clues.revealExplanation: The Wars of the Roses were fought over the badge, and a warhorse is what they were fought on.

blindReview.reason: War horse is a stock phrase and the War(s) of the Roses is well known from history and the film title.

clues.wordAConnection: The Kentucky Derby is a horse race.
clues.wordBConnection: It is known as the Run for the Roses.
clues.revealExplanation: The Kentucky Derby is a horse race known as the Run for the Roses.

blindReview.reason: Derby is a horse race; the Kentucky Derby's 'Run for the Roses' is a detail only fans know.

clues.wordAConnection: The winning horse is draped in one.
clues.wordBConnection: And it is woven out of roses.
clues.revealExplanation: The winning horse is draped in a blanket of roses.

blindReview.reason: Horse blanket is fine, but the Derby's 'blanket of roses' is trivia a stranger will not reach.

pairs.pairNote: ELSA and FROZEN are both clean (one film); SNOW passes via the Snow Queen title; ARENDELLE is correct but moderate recognizability; CHESS and CUBE are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: Elsa's ice magic.
clues.wordBConnection: Elsa is the queen of Arendelle.
clues.revealExplanation: Elsa, Frozen's ice queen.

blindReview.reason: Elsa from Frozen has ice magic and is crowned Queen of Arendelle; a household name.

clues.wordAConnection: Frozen solid: ice.
clues.wordBConnection: Frozen, the film about Queen Elsa.
clues.revealExplanation: Frozen: ice, and the film about a queen.

blindReview.reason: Frozen is the plain state of ice and the Disney film whose heroine becomes queen; the film is broadly known.

clues.wordAConnection: Snow and ice.
clues.wordBConnection: The Snow Queen.
clues.revealExplanation: The Snow Queen.

blindReview.reason: Snow sits next to ice; 'Snow Queen' (Andersen, Narnia, Frozen's source) is a known title, a solid second reach.
Arendelle is the kingdom in Frozen ruled by the ice-powered Queen Elsa; accurate, but the name is known mainly to Frozen fans and parents.

provenance.authorReason: generic: ICE only, and fits half the board

blindReview.reason: Cold is the property of ice; the 'ice queen' idiom for an aloof woman is the only route to QUEEN, and that route goes through the other target rather than a 'cold queen' compound.
The queen is a chess piece; chess has no ice sense.
Ice cube is direct; nothing regal about a cube.

pairs.pairNote: CAST is the elegant double meaning and HEAVY the sturdy antonym; GLOW is light-only.

clues.wordAConnection: Iron is the byword for heavy.
clues.wordBConnection: Light is its exact opposite.
clues.revealExplanation: Iron is the byword for heavy and light is its exact opposite.

blindReview.reason: Iron is heavy and heavy is the opposite of light.

clues.wordAConnection: Cast iron is the material.
clues.wordBConnection: Light is cast across a room.
clues.revealExplanation: Cast iron is the material and light is cast across a room.

blindReview.reason: Cast iron and cast light are both standard collocations.

clues.wordAConnection: Iron glows when it is heated.
clues.wordBConnection: Which is light coming straight out of the metal.
clues.revealExplanation: Iron glows when it is heated, which is light coming straight out of the metal.

blindReview.reason: Light glows; hot iron glowing is true but needs the player to picture a forge.

pairs.pairNote: MAP is a neat double meaning and PRESS a good plain-sense hint; GARDEN is rose-only.

clues.wordAConnection: Every map carries a key to read it by.
clues.wordBConnection: And a compass rose to point it north.
clues.revealExplanation: Every map carries a key to read it by and a compass rose to point it north.

blindReview.reason: A map has a key (legend) and a compass rose; both are standard map vocabulary.

clues.wordAConnection: You press a key.
clues.wordBConnection: You press a rose flat between the pages of a book.
clues.revealExplanation: You press a key and you press a rose flat between the pages of a book.

blindReview.reason: You press a key, and pressing a rose in a book is a familiar keepsake practice.

clues.wordAConnection: In The Secret Garden a buried key unlocks the door.
clues.wordBConnection: And the walled garden behind it is full of roses.
clues.revealExplanation: In The Secret Garden a buried key unlocks the walled garden full of roses.

blindReview.reason: Rose garden is direct, but nothing leads from garden to key short of The Secret Garden's locked door.

pairs.pairNote: WIND is the one hint that reaches both words from a single wind-up image; CLOCK is the same idea one step further away.

clues.wordAConnection: You wind it using a key.
clues.wordBConnection: And what you are winding is a clockwork spring.
clues.revealExplanation: You wind a clockwork spring using a key.

blindReview.reason: You wind a clock or toy with a key, which tightens its spring; spring breezes give a second route.

clues.wordAConnection: A key is what releases it.
clues.wordBConnection: A lock is a spring-loaded mechanism.
clues.revealExplanation: A lock is a spring-loaded mechanism and a key is what releases it.

blindReview.reason: Lock and key is immediate; a spring-loaded lock is mechanical detail.

clues.wordAConnection: A clock is wound with a key.
clues.wordBConnection: And driven by a spring.
clues.revealExplanation: A clock is driven by a spring and wound with a key.

blindReview.reason: A wind-up clock has a key and a mainspring, but neither is the first thing a player thinks of for clock.

pairs.pairNote: MUFASA and SIMBA are both clean (same film); JUNGLE rides one universal idiom; THRONE and CROWN are king-side words with only a heraldic reach to the lion.

clues.wordAConnection: Mufasa is the king of the Pride Lands.
clues.wordBConnection: Mufasa is a lion.
clues.revealExplanation: Mufasa, the lion king in The Lion King.

blindReview.reason: Mufasa is the reigning king in The Lion King and is a lion; both sides are immediate for anyone who knows the film.

clues.wordAConnection: Simba grows up to be king.
clues.wordBConnection: Simba is a lion.
clues.revealExplanation: Simba, the lion who becomes king in The Lion King.

blindReview.reason: Simba is the lion cub who becomes king in The Lion King; the film title itself carries both words.

clues.wordAConnection: The king of the jungle.
clues.wordBConnection: That king is the lion.
clues.revealExplanation: The lion is the king of the jungle.

blindReview.reason: The stock phrase 'king of the jungle' names the lion; KING is reached through that same idiom, which is universal.

provenance.authorReason: reaches KING only; Pride Rock is a stretch

blindReview.reason: A throne is a king's seat; lions reach it only via heraldry or Pride Rock in The Lion King, which needs explaining.

provenance.authorReason: KING only; also a board word that would be a target elsewhere

blindReview.reason: Crown is the king's emblem; the crowned heraldic lion (as on the English royal arms) is a stretch for most players.

clues.wordAConnection: Narnia's true king is Aslan.
clues.wordBConnection: Aslan is a lion.
clues.revealExplanation: Aslan the lion is the king of Narnia.

blindReview.reason: Aslan the lion is Narnia's best-known figure via 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe'; KING requires knowing Aslan rules Narnia or that the children become kings and queens.
A mane is the lion's defining feature; nothing about it points to a king.
Lions roar; kings do not, and no idiom or compound bridges the gap.

pairs.pairNote: DARK and BLACK both work through a famous Knight compound plus a plain night sense; MARE passes on the nightmare compound; ARMOR and OWL are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: The Black Knight.
clues.wordBConnection: A black night.
clues.revealExplanation: The Black Knight; a black night.

blindReview.reason: Judged as compounds: 'Black Knight' (Arthurian legend, Monty Python, the Marvel character) on one side and 'black as night' / 'black night' on the other; both are established phrases.

clues.wordAConnection: The Dark Knight.
clues.wordBConnection: A dark night.
clues.revealExplanation: The Dark Knight, and a dark night.

blindReview.reason: Dark is the plain property of night, and 'The Dark Knight' (Batman) is a household title.

clues.wordAConnection: A knight rides a mare.
clues.wordBConnection: A nightmare.
clues.revealExplanation: A knight's mare, and a nightmare.

blindReview.reason: Night + mare makes nightmare; a mare is a horse, the knight's mount and the shape of the chess knight, so KNIGHT is a solid second reach.

provenance.authorReason: knight in shining armour reaches KNIGHT only

blindReview.reason: 'Knight in shining armor' is immediate; stars shining at night is a soft reach and 'shining night' is not a compound.
Armor is knight equipment with no night sense.
Owls are the nocturnal emblem of night; nothing links them to knights.

pairs.pairNote: CAST is the elegant answer and DARK the blunt one; PUPPET and SUN lean on the shadow or light side respectively.

clues.wordAConnection: Light is what casts it.
clues.wordBConnection: And the thing cast is a shadow.
clues.revealExplanation: Light is what casts a shadow.

blindReview.reason: You cast a shadow and cast light on something; both collocations are everyday.

clues.wordAConnection: Dark is what light is not.
clues.wordBConnection: A shadow is a patch of it.
clues.revealExplanation: A shadow is a patch of dark and dark is what light is not.

blindReview.reason: Dark is the direct opposite of light and the substance of a shadow; generic but natural to both.

clues.wordAConnection: Shadow puppets need a lamp behind them.
clues.wordBConnection: And what reaches the screen is nothing but shadow.
clues.revealExplanation: Shadow puppets work by putting a hand between a lamp and the screen.

blindReview.reason: Shadow puppet is direct; the lamp behind the puppet is a second step most players will not make unprompted.

clues.wordAConnection: The sun is the light.
clues.wordBConnection: And it is what puts shadows on the ground.
clues.revealExplanation: The sun is the light that puts shadows on the ground.

blindReview.reason: Sunlight is immediate; sun to shadow requires thinking about what the sun produces behind an object.

pairs.pairNote: TIDE is excellent and BLUE is a natural colour hint for both; PULL is the tide idea without the word; the rest are one-sided.

clues.wordAConnection: Once in a blue moon.
clues.wordBConnection: The blue ocean.
clues.revealExplanation: A blue moon over the blue ocean.

provenance.authorReason: blue moon is a phrase, blue ocean is a colour: generic colour clue

blindReview.reason: 'Blue moon' is a common idiom and the ocean is the archetypal blue thing; both sides are direct.

clues.wordAConnection: The moon's pull makes the tide.
clues.wordBConnection: The ocean's tide.
clues.revealExplanation: The moon pulls the ocean's tides.

blindReview.reason: Tides belong to the ocean and are commonly known to be caused by the moon.
The moon's gravitational pull drives the ocean's tides, but both words need that explanation; PULL alone is abstract.
Ocean floor is a set phrase; 'moon floor' is not.
'The deep' is the ocean; the moon is not described as deep.
Craters are the moon's surface feature; no ocean sense.

pairs.pairNote: HOWL is the clean two-way hint and NIGHT is a natural shared setting; CRY and FULL each lean on one side; PACK is wolf-only.

clues.wordAConnection: Howling at the moon.
clues.wordBConnection: The wolf's howl.
clues.revealExplanation: A wolf howls at the moon.

blindReview.reason: Wolves howl, and 'howl at the moon' is a stock phrase.

clues.wordAConnection: The moon rules the night.
clues.wordBConnection: The wolf is a creature of the night.
clues.revealExplanation: Both belong to the night.

blindReview.reason: The moon belongs to the night, and the wolf is culturally a creature of the night (howling in the dark, werewolf lore); natural to both.

provenance.authorReason: weaker form of HOWL and one-sided

blindReview.reason: 'Cry wolf' is a common idiom; MOON only arrives if the player pictures a wolf crying at the moon, and 'cry moon' is not a compound.

clues.wordAConnection: A full moon.
clues.wordBConnection: The werewolf of the full moon.
clues.revealExplanation: The full moon that makes the werewolf.

blindReview.reason: Full moon is immediate; WOLF follows only through the werewolf idea, which rides on the moon side.
Wolf pack is direct; there is no moon sense.

pairs.pairNote: BLOOM and BUD are both strong but are the same flowering idea; GARDEN leans toward rose.

clues.wordAConnection: Roses bloom.
clues.wordBConnection: Spring is when.
clues.revealExplanation: Roses bloom when spring arrives.

blindReview.reason: Roses bloom and spring is the season of bloom.

clues.wordAConnection: A rosebud is the unopened flower.
clues.wordBConnection: Budding is what everything does in spring.
clues.revealExplanation: A rosebud is the unopened flower and budding is what everything does in spring.

blindReview.reason: Rosebud is a word and buds appear in spring.

clues.wordAConnection: Roses are what the garden is planted with.
clues.wordBConnection: Spring is when it comes back.
clues.revealExplanation: The spring garden is where the roses are.

blindReview.reason: Rose garden is direct; spring gardening is a seasonal association rather than a phrase, so the spring side is the weak one, not the generic-ness.
